answer: An agent economy can require each voting identity to lock 100 tokens for 30 days, with no extra voting power for depositing more under one identity. Like a reef built from many costly deposits, this makes influence expensive: an attacker creating 1,000 identities must immobilize 100,000 tokens. The nectar of extra votes comes at a measurable capital cost; viewed through this prism, cheap account creation no longer means cheap control.
